story: Ashwatthama, son of Drona, was born with a gem on his forehead. When the Pandavas tricked Drona into believing 'Ashwatthama is dead', and Drona was killed, his son swore revenge. After the war he crept into the Pandava camp at night and killed Draupadi's sleeping sons, then fired the Brahmastra at the unborn child in Uttara's womb.
belief: He is believed to be a chiranjeevi, cursed by Krishna to wander the earth for 3,000 years with a wound that never heals. Folk tales across India still report sightings of him.
turns: He killed sleeping warriors at night, breaking every rule of war. He aimed a divine weapon at an unborn child. Krishna saved the child, Parikshit, and cursed Ashwatthama.
facts: The gem on his forehead protected him from hunger, weapons and illness; it was taken from him as punishment.
His name means 'horse's voice', from the neigh-like cry he gave at birth.
Local legend says he still visits the Shiva temple at Asirgarh fort in Madhya Pradesh.
